title: Allowlisted precompiled worker module loader
objective: Load the explicitly precompiled maximal-order worker module graph in lightweight multiprocessing evaluators without a parser, compiler, or arbitrary filesystem lookup, and reject unknown or uncompiled modules with Windows/SEA-safe fallback semantics

handoff.summary: Added a fail-closed resource manifest and genuinely on-demand loader for build-precompiled multiprocessing modules, an exact read-only capability query, portable virtual filenames, and focused synthetic loader/rejection coverage. Workers read only the manifest at startup and fetch an exact validated module resource on first import. The explicit maximal-order portfolio emits 33 authorized modules; its four-prime Round2 public worker run is exactly sequential-equivalent. Ordinary builds without the optional graph retain self-contained Pool behavior and report the module capability as false. Focused loader tests also pass on native Windows x64.
risks: The full multiprocessing test passed 9 of 10 cases here; its advanced elliptic case and several portable-tier tests require the optional FLINT addon and development headers, which this isolated worktree does not have installed.
The required architecture receipt reaches the native audit but fails on an inherited generated native-export inventory drift outside this lane's claims.
The portable tier also reports the newly inherited public-worker test is absent from the shared test-tier manifest; that manifest belongs to the arithmetic integration lane.
next_steps: Exercise the emitted task graph in a single-executable build; its resource lookup uses the same authoritative SEA asset map as other lazy caches.
